column1: # Game profile of Sea of Stars (Switch, update 2.0.59001 = v786432). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2021.3.25f1 (IL2CPP) with Wwise, SDK 16.2.0 (its sdk is Super Mario Bros. Wonder 1.0.0's build); subsdk0 is the movie module (the cinematics are MP4s in StreamingAssets).
# The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the player's serialized files and the 1,126 bundles in StreamingAssets, read by unityfs.py (3,887 of the 3,898; 11 are the player's
# GLSLC outputs in main); no run met a shader missing from the map.
# The game asks for present interval 1 and runs at 60 fps as on the Switch

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x8b66a0) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as one
# address region and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The sdk build takes the node area cut and the 2 MB region alignment of SDK 20 (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py). The 5 GB block of Ace Attorney
# Investigations Collection (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region) with a 1.5 GB pool: StandardAllocator reserves 1.44 GB and commits about
# 0.7 GB in the prologue (measured with a 64 GB alias region); Unity's own regions hold about 1.15 GB more. With the hardware pool (3.2 GB) Unity got no region within 6 minutes
# (a write at NULL + 0x3fffe0); with the 1.5 GB pool and the cut the alias region's high-water mark stays at +3.0 GB over 20 minutes, 2.6 GB of it in live regions
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles
